title: Milestone 2026.04.64 Operational Retrospective — Full Analysis (Augmented)
augmentation_note: Conductor-generated Exp 842 artifact covers only the managed conductor cycle (11 experiments, 218 min). This file is the authoritative full-milestone retro, augmented with user-provided timing data: 3971 min, 750 experiments. Baseline comparison: .63 (3904 min, 728 experiments) is the prior full-milestone retro; .58 (3415 min, 612 experiments) is the improvement-streak baseline.
experiment_count_vs_cap: 750 vs 700 cap — EXCEEDED by 50 experiments (+22 this milestone, cumulative overage growing each cycle)
streak_note: Fifth consecutive full-milestone wall-time regression (.60: +241 min vs .58, .61: +273 min vs .58, .62: +386 min vs .58, .63: +489 min vs .58, .64: +556 min vs .58). Regression vs .58 continues to widen. Per-experiment average TICKED UP to 5.29 min from the 5.0 floor held in .61/.62/.63 — the first per-experiment regression in four milestones. This suggests the experiment composition is shifting toward more complex, longer-running items even as total experiment count grows. The structural regression from count growth (+22 this milestone) combined with per-experiment regression creates a compounding problem.
headline_finding: FIFTH CONSECUTIVE FULL-MILESTONE WALL-TIME REGRESSION: +67 min (+1.7%) vs .63 (3904 min), +556 min (+16.3%) vs .58 baseline (3415 min). UNPRECEDENTED^4 — SLOWEST-5 IDENTICAL FOR FIVE CONSECUTIVE MILESTONES: Exp 786, 527, 491, 627, 603 appear for the FIFTH consecutive time unchanged (.60, .61, .62, .63, .64). A four-milestone freeze was unprecedented^3 in .63 — five consecutive is unprecedented^4. DOCUMENTATION-WITHOUT-APPLICATION LOOP NOW IN 6TH CONSECUTIVE MILESTONE: the same improvement actions (manifest enforcement, timeout watchdog, DualGPU migration, paragraph batching, experiment count cap) have been written in .58, .60, .61, .62, .63, and .64 retros without implementation for the non-conductor queue. RETRO-SYMCODE-SERIAL CLOSED BUT EXP 627 STILL RAN: The most damning finding — paragraph batching was implemented and validated at 1.710x speedup (Exp 841), RETRO-SYMCODE-SERIAL was CLOSED, yet Exp 627 STILL ran at 51 min in the full-milestone queue. This proves the manifest is the root cause: fixing the implementation without fixing the dispatch site produces zero wall-time improvement. PER-EXPERIMENT REGRESSION: avg 5.29 min vs .63's 5.0 min floor — first per-experiment regression in four milestones, signaling experiment complexity drift. EXPERIMENT COUNT 750: exceeds 700 cap by 50 experiments, the largest overage in project history. GPU CLOSE: 47C/46C (1C differential), still very clean — GPU Zombie Killer and RETRO-028 closure holding.

bottlenecks_identified: UNPRECEDENTED^4 — SLOWEST-5 IDENTICAL FOR FIVE CONSECUTIVE MILESTONES (.60-.61-.62-.63-.64): Exp 786, 527, 491, 627, 603 appear unchanged for the fifth time. In .63 we noted a four-consecutive freeze was unprecedented^3. Five consecutive is unprecedented^4. This is a mathematical certainty under the current architecture: same unguarded queue sources, same absent manifest checks, same absent timeout watchdogs. The five experiments have collectively consumed ~1,130 min across the five milestone period. At 5 experiments × 5 milestones × average 55 min = 1,375 min of structurally preventable overhead.

DOCUMENTATION-WITHOUT-APPLICATION LOOP NOW IN 6TH CONSECUTIVE MILESTONE: Core actions (manifest enforcement, timeout watchdog, DualGPU migration, paragraph batching, experiment count cap) have been written in .58, .60, .61, .62, .63, AND .64 retros without full-milestone implementation. Six consecutive milestones of non-implementation is definitive evidence the retro-to-action pipeline is architecturally broken. The retro document functions as an analytical archive, not a change-management system. Voluntary recommendations are never actioned. Hard gates are the only intervention with a track record of producing change.

EXP 627 PROOF OF CONCEPT — IMPLEMENTATION WITHOUT MANIFEST = ZERO SAVINGS: RETRO-SYMCODE-SERIAL was closed in .64 (Exp 841, 1.710x speedup validated). Yet Exp 627 ran at 51 min unchanged. This is a controlled experiment in the failure mode: the fix was applied to the new experiment (Exp 841) but not to the manifest/dispatch of the old experiment. The old Exp 627 continued to run from the unguarded queue. This definitively proves manifest enforcement is the load-bearing fix, not the implementation fix. Without manifest enforcement, any efficiency improvement exists only in the conductor cycle and never propagates to the full-milestone queue.

EXP 786 — TWO CONSECUTIVE POST-RETRO028-CLOSURE APPEARANCES (154 min cumulative waste): RETRO-028 was closed in .62. Exp 786 ran for 77 min in BOTH .63 and .64 with zero research value. Cumulative waste from two post-closure milestones: 154 min. Nine consecutive retro recommendations for the same 30-60 minute code fix. ROI calculation: 30-60 min engineering time → 77 min/milestone forever. The investment pays back in under one milestone.

EXP 527 — 11th+ POST-RETIREMENT APPEARANCE (572+ min cumulative post-retirement waste): Retired in .57. Nine consecutive retro recommendations for the same fix. Cumulative post-retirement waste ~572 min (9.5 hours). The engineering team has spent more time writing about this fix than it would take to implement it by a factor of at least 10x.

EXPERIMENT COUNT AT HISTORIC HIGH — 750 vs 700 CAP (50 EXPERIMENTS OVER): 750 experiments in .64 vs 728 (.63), +22 this milestone. Cap is 700 — exceeded by 50 experiments, the largest overage in project history. Per-experiment avg ticked UP to 5.29 min (from 5.0 floor). At 5.29 min/experiment, the 50-experiment overage alone represents 264 min of structural overhead. At current growth rate (+22/milestone), the count will reach 800 in ~2 milestones and wall time will exceed 4,200 min.

PER-EXPERIMENT AVERAGE REGRESSION: First per-experiment uptick in four milestones — 5.29 min vs 5.0 min floor in .61/.62/.63. This signals experiment complexity drift (more GPU-heavy, longer-running experiments entering the queue) while retirement of shorter experiments lags. Combined with count growth, this compounds the wall-time regression beyond what count growth alone would predict.

GPU UTILIZATION — SEQUENTIAL EXECUTION PERSISTS: Both GPUs closed at 47C/46C (1C differential, clean). GPU Zombie Killer working. DualGPU ThreadPoolExecutor validated at 1.8319x speedup (Exp 746, .57) remains unapplied to Exp 603/491-class across SEVEN consecutive milestones. GPU utilization pattern remains: full load during inference, 0% between experiments, no concurrent training+inference pipeline.

JEPA OOD AUC RECOVERY STALLED: Exp 834 (JEPA v24 DG-PRM reweighting) lifted ARC AUC from 0.04 to 0.72 but SVAMP collapsed to 0.0 (RETRO-SVAMP-ZERO-AUC). min_domain_auc=0.0 blocked deployment (Exp 838). ARBITER STILL NON-FUNCTIONAL: RETRO-ARBITER-FLAT-ENERGY (opened .62). Exp 835 Z-score normalization did not fix accuracy_standard=0.0. Multi-Agent Arbiter has been non-functional for two consecutive milestones (.62, .63, .64). Zero capability delivered despite three experiments targeted at the issue.

CONSTRAINT RETRIEVAL STILL BROKEN: RETRO-CONSTRAINT-ZERO-DELTA. Exp 836 fixed the write path (15 constraints stored) but delta_overall=0.0 still. Retrieval path broken. Three milestones since root cause identified.

improvements_suggested.rationale: Nine consecutive retro recommendations for the same 30-60 minute fix. The Exp 627 case in .64 proved that even when the underlying implementation is fixed (RETRO-SYMCODE-SERIAL closed), the old experiment still runs from the unguarded queue. Manifest enforcement is the load-bearing fix for the entire documentation-without-application loop.

Without this wiring, Exp 627 will continue to run at 51 min from the unguarded queue for the sixth consecutive milestone despite the implementation being deployed.

The old experiment must be explicitly retired from all queue sources and the new implementation substituted. This is a 30-minute wiring task, not a research task.

This unblocks the Arbiter and FR-11 Tier 1 relay cascade.

improvements_suggested.action: Reduce iCE40 Ising sampler to N=16 spins for bitstream generation (RETRO-ICE40-PNR-LUT-OVERFLOW): Exp 839 N=32 (3952 LUTs) exceeded HX8K P&R budget. N=16 targets ~1000 LUTs — well within HX8K capacity. Run nextpnr-ice40 with --hx8k --package ct256. Gate: bitstream_generated=True AND bitstream_valid_header=True. KV260 FPGA board has been idle since arrival 2026-04-20.

N=16 is mathematically sufficient for the energy sampling proof-of-concept. Five experiments have targeted FPGA synthesis without producing a working bitstream.

improvements_suggested.action: Add SVAMP domain triplets to JEPA v24b training corpus (RETRO-SVAMP-ZERO-AUC): Exp 834 DG-PRM reweighting lifted ARC from 0.04 to 0.72 but SVAMP collapsed to 0.0. SVAMP was not in training corpus. Add 20 SVAMP triplets with PRM reward labels. Gate: auc_svamp >= 0.40 on SVAMP holdout. Deploy as JEPA v24b, target min_domain_auc >= 0.50 across all domains to unblock Exp 838-class deployment.

JEPA deployment has been blocked for 10+ consecutive retrain attempts. Per-domain floor is the correct gate — it just needs data coverage to pass.

improvements_suggested.action: Fix MultiAgentArbiter energy calibration (RETRO-ARBITER-FLAT-ENERGY): Exp 835 Z-score normalization did not fix accuracy_standard=0.0. energies_raw show near-zero magnitudes consistent with unconverged MCMC. Fix: warm-start Gibbs sampler from external-field aligned configuration s_i=sign(h_i) with 500 burn-in steps. Gate: accuracy_overall >= 0.60.
improvements_suggested.rationale: Three milestones since the arbiter was first deployed as non-functional. Warm-start is a known MCMC technique that addresses convergence failure. Zero capability delivered from a deployed component.

improvements_suggested.action: Migrate Exp 603 and Exp 491-class to DualGPU ThreadPoolExecutor: Both GPUs at 47C/46C (1C differential), GPU 1 fully available with RETRO-028 closed. DualGPU speedup validated at 1.8319x (Exp 746). Exp 603 (44 min) → ~24 min. Exp 491-class (52 min) → ~26 min or retire if JEPA clears 0.75 gate. Combined savings: ~45 min/milestone.
improvements_suggested.rationale: Seven consecutive milestones since DualGPU speedup validation with no systematic migration. GPU 1 availability is at its highest in project history. This is the highest-value optimization remaining after manifest enforcement.

improvements_suggested.action: Deploy ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog as mandatory infrastructure (CARNOT_EXPERIMENT_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=30): Exp 786 (77 min), Exp 491 (52 min), Exp 627 (51 min), Exp 603 (44 min) all ran unbounded for FIVE consecutive milestones. ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog exists in codebase but deployment is optional. Set default timeout to 30 min with checkpoint saves at timeout. This is the backstop for manifest enforcement failures: even if a retired experiment re-enters the queue, it cannot exceed 30 min.
improvements_suggested.rationale: Manifest enforcement is the primary fix. The timeout watchdog is the defense-in-depth backstop. If manifest enforcement fails (as it has for six consecutive milestones), the watchdog caps the damage. Both layers are needed.

Soft suggestions are never actioned (six consecutive milestones of proof). MILESTONE_PREREQS.md must list every IMMEDIATE action, be signed off, and be verified before the conductor dequeues any .65 experiment.
improvements_suggested.rationale: This converts retro text into an execution prerequisite. The documentation-without-application loop cannot persist if experiments are blocked until retro actions are signed off.

answers_to_key_questions.q1_slowest_experiments_why: All five slowest experiments are structural carryovers from unguarded historical queues — five consecutive identical appearances, unprecedented^4. Exp 786 (77 min): resolved OOM investigation for RETRO-028 (closed .62) — zero research value for two consecutive milestones, re-executed purely because the manifest check is missing at non-conductor dequeue sites. Exp 527 (52 min): retired in .57, now in its 11th+ post-retirement appearance. Exp 491 (52 min): JEPA diagnostic whose root cause was identified externally, potentially superseded by ongoing JEPA v24 work. Exp 627 (51 min): The most important case — RETRO-SYMCODE-SERIAL was CLOSED in .64 (paragraph batching implemented, 1.710x speedup), yet Exp 627 ran at 51 min unchanged. This proves the dispatch site is the actual bottleneck. Exp 603 (44 min): Productive research that DualGPU migration would reduce by 45%; seven consecutive milestones since speedup validation with no migration.
answers_to_key_questions.q2_gpu_utilization: Adequate at close (47C/46C, 1C differential), still sequentially executed. GPU close is clean: 4MB/0% on both GPUs. GPU Zombie Killer working correctly. RETRO-028 closure confirmed stable. DualGPU ThreadPoolExecutor validated at 1.8319x speedup remains unapplied for Exp 603/491-class across seven consecutive milestones. Both GPUs idle at close per GPU monitor — the DualGPU runner suggestion ('Use DualGPURunner to run Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1 simultaneously') has appeared in consecutive GPU monitor reports without triggering a code change. GPU utilization pattern: full load during inference, 0% between experiments, no concurrent training+inference.
answers_to_key_questions.q3_zombie_processes: None detected. GPU Zombie Killer (Exp 780) is working correctly. Both GPUs at 4MB/0% at close — driver-level context allocations only. Clean close maintained. RETRO-028 closure (Exp 810, .62) continues to hold — no VRAM leaks. This is the healthiest component of the infrastructure.
answers_to_key_questions.q4_parallelization_opportunities: Three high-value opportunities remain unexploited: (1) DualGPU ThreadPoolExecutor for Exp 603 (training) + GPU 0 (inference) — 1.8319x speedup validated in .57, never applied to these experiments across seven milestones; (2) CPU+GPU parallel: CPU-bound experiments (spec coverage check, type-check, constraint mining) can run concurrently with GPU inference during model load time — this is the lowest-effort parallelization gain; (3) Pytest-xdist for pre-flight test suite parallelization — at 750 experiments the test suite scales proportionally and represents 15-16% of wall time at 1 min/test, parallelization to 4x would save ~200 min.
answers_to_key_questions.q5_preflight_bottleneck: Growing. At 750 experiments the pre-flight test suite has grown proportionally. Incremental test selection in the conductor cycle reduces this for managed experiments, but full-milestone pre-flight runs against the entire corpus. Pytest-xdist parallel execution is the highest-leverage pre-flight optimization. Alternatively, reducing experiment count to 700 cap would directly reduce test suite size by 50 experiments (~50 min at 1 min/test).
answers_to_key_questions.q6_doc_reconciliation_efficiency: Efficient and not a bottleneck. Planning sessions (arxiv scan + experiment design + roadmap writing) complete in ~1-2 hours per milestone. Conductor cycle doc updates take <15 minutes per experiment. The inefficiency is structural: the retro process produces accurate, detailed documentation but the documentation is not connected to a change-management system. Six consecutive milestones of documentation-without-application. The retro process itself is fast; the gap is the retro-to-action pipeline.
answers_to_key_questions.q7_tooling_infrastructure_changes: Eight changes would have the largest cumulative impact: (1) Manifest enforcement at ALL dequeue sites — eliminates Exp 527 + Exp 786 immediately + enables Exp 627 old-version retirement; (2) Retire old Exp 627 + wire batched replacement — completes RETRO-SYMCODE-SERIAL implementation (fix deployed, deployment wiring missing); (3) Mandatory experiment retirement sweep (retire 50+ to return to 700 cap) — 264 min savings at 5.29 min/experiment; (4) MILESTONE_PREREQS.md hard-blocking gate — structural gate preventing experiments from running until IMMEDIATE retro actions are signed off; (5) ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog mandatory deployment — caps unbounded experiments at 30 min; (6) DualGPU ThreadPoolExecutor migration for Exp 603/491-class; (7) Pytest-xdist pre-flight test parallelization; (8) Constraint retrieval fix → enables arbiter calibration → unblocks FR-11 Tier 1 cascade.
